description: project settings.json has a non-empty permissions.allow list
command: jq -e '.permissions.allow | length > 0' .claude/settings.json >/dev/null && echo pass || echo fail

description: project settings.json denies rm -rf and terraform destroy
command: jq -e '(.permissions.deny | index("Bash(rm -rf:*)")) and (.permissions.deny | index("Bash(terraform destroy:*)"))' .claude/settings.json >/dev/null && echo pass || echo fail

description: workspace trust is accepted so project allow rules load

deny overrides allow: with rm both allowed AND denied the agent is refused (victim survives), while a control run with rm only allowed really does delete — so this passes only when the agent actually ran
command: V=$(mktemp -t m2victim.XXXXXX); W=$(mktemp -t m2ctl.XXXXXX); printf '{"permissions":{"allow":["Bash(rm:*)"]}}' > .claude/settings.local.json; timeout 120 claude -p "Run exactly: rm $W — reply RAN or BLOCKED." --permission-mode auto </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; printf '{"permissions":{"allow":["Bash(rm:*)"],"deny":["Bash(rm:*)"]}}' > .claude/settings.local.json; timeout 120 claude -p "Run exactly: rm $V — reply RAN or BLOCKED." --permission-mode auto </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -f .claude/settings.local.json; if [ -f "$W" ]; then rm -f "$V" "$W"; echo "fail: control run did not delete — the agent never executed, so the deny result proves nothing"; exit 0; fi; [ -f "$V" ] && { rm -f "$V"; echo pass; } || echo fail

description: Bash sandbox blocks outbound network fail-closed: curl to an external host fails inside the sandbox (non-zero exit), while a control write inside the workspace succeeds — so this passes only when the agent actually ran
command: rm -f ./m2-sbx-control.txt ./m2-sbx-net.err; printf '{"sandbox":{"enabled":true}}' > .claude/settings.local.json; timeout 120 claude -p "Run exactly: echo sandbox-control > ./m2-sbx-control.txt — reply RAN or BLOCKED." --permission-mode dontAsk </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; timeout 120 claude -p "Run exactly: curl -sS --max-time 5 https://example.com > /dev/null 2> ./m2-sbx-net.err; echo rc=\$? >> ./m2-sbx-net.err — then reply DONE." --permission-mode dontAsk </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -f .claude/settings.local.json; if [ ! -f ./m2-sbx-control.txt ]; then rm -f ./m2-sbx-net.err; echo "fail: control write did not happen — the agent never executed, so the network result proves nothing"; exit 0; fi; rm -f ./m2-sbx-control.txt; if grep -q "rc=0" ./m2-sbx-net.err 2>/dev/null; then rm -f ./m2-sbx-net.err; echo fail; else rm -f ./m2-sbx-net.err; echo pass; fi

description: YOUR POLICY: agentops/posture-policy.md exists — the module ships a written posture policy, not just an understanding of one
YOUR POLICY: the policy names the postures it assigns — plan, acceptEdits and auto all appear, so each task class resolves to a concrete mode rather than a vague trust level
command: F=agentops/posture-policy.md; [ -f "$F" ] || { echo fail; exit 0; }; grep -qi 'plan' "$F" && grep -qi 'acceptEdits' "$F" && grep -qi 'auto' "$F" && echo pass || echo fail

description: YOUR POLICY: the policy records that deny rules hold regardless of posture — the Step 3 result written down, so nobody later reads deny as a preference rather than an override
command: F=agentops/posture-policy.md; [ -f "$F" ] || { echo fail; exit 0; }; grep -qi 'deny' "$F" && grep -qiE 'regardless|override|beats|always|cannot be' "$F" && echo pass || echo fail
